title: Sales Enablement: Positioning, Competitive Briefs, Pricing Guidance, Case Studies, and Security FAQ
author: Ava Thompson
summary: This playbook bundles Redwood Inference's recommended positioning and messaging, concise competitive briefs, a pitch-deck outline, pricing guidance, representative case studies, and an FAQ for security-conscious prospects. Intended audience: field sales, solutions engineering (SE), and customer-facing product leaders. Use this as the primary single-page reference during discovery, proposal drafting, and executive briefings.
positioning_and_messaging:
Purpose:
- Provide repeatable, engineering-forward messaging that emphasizes Redwood's production-first inference platform and operational economics.

Core elevator pitch (30s):
- Redwood Inference is a developer-first inference platform that makes high-performance LLM serving predictable and economical across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. We reduce your inference unit costs with smart batching, caching, and model routing while giving teams enterprise controls (SLA, VPC/private deployment, audit logs).

Top value props (customer-facing):
- Predictable performance: SLA-backed Dedicated capacity and consistent latency across deployments.
- Cost efficiency: Automatic batching, KV caching, and guided quantization profiles that reduce per-token cost.
- Flexible deployment: Hosted API for quick wins, Dedicated for scale, and Private for regulated workloads.
- Developer-first UX: Familiar REST/SDK, streaming responses, function/tool calling, and detailed observability dashboards.

ICP (ideal customer profile):
- AI-native startups and product teams that need low-latency chat and generation at scale.
- Mid-market/enterprise teams requiring SLAs, data isolation, and compliance controls.
- Platform teams standardizing inference across business units.

Common objections & recommended responses:
1) "We can self-host cheaper."  Response: Outline total cost of ownership, ramp complexity, and hidden operational burden. Highlight our Reserved Dedicated pricing and Optimize tooling that reduces unit cost via batching/quantization without sacrificing quality.
2) "We need on-prem for compliance."  Response: Explain Redwood Private (VPC + optional on-prem package), KMS/HSM integrations, audit logging, and our professional services to accelerate on-prem setups.
3) "Model quality/regressions are risky."  Response: Show model catalog, Redwood-verified performance profiles, built-in evals and regression alerts tied to prompt sets, and canary/rollout controls.

Key metrics to cite in conversations:
- Median p99 latency for common configs (example: 32-token prompt on g4dn-like hardware): 120ms (hosted).
- Typical unit cost improvements from caching + batching: 2-5x depending on workload.
- SLA: 99.9% uptime for Dedicated (example contract).
competitive_briefs:
Overview:
- Use the competitor briefs below as 1-paragraph summaries with recommended battle cards for common objections. Update vendor details quarterly.

Competitor: LargeCloudAI
- Summary: Large public cloud provider with managed model endpoints and broad ecosystem integration. Strengths: global regions, integrated data services, deep security. Weaknesses: higher per-token costs for small/medium workloads, less opinionated inference optimizations, slower release cycles for model-specific kernel optimizations.
- Win themes vs LargeCloudAI: Lower unit costs for production LLM workloads, faster inference tuning, and more developer-friendly SDKs for rapid iteration.

Competitor: InferenceCo (self-hosted runtime vendor)
- Summary: Focused on on-prem/self-managed runtimes with strong kernel-level optimizations. Strengths: complete control, potentially lower raw GPU cost. Weaknesses: operational complexity, limited observability and rollouts, longer integration time.
- Win themes vs InferenceCo: Offer turnkey Dedicated and Private deployments with Redwood-managed control plane, integrated rollout tooling, and usage-based pricing to reduce initial commitment.

Competitor: LLM-API-Provider
- Summary: API-first providers that emphasize simplicity and wide model access. Strengths: easy onboarding, generous free tiers. Weaknesses: less focus on enterprise SLA/controls and limited private deployment options.
- Win themes: Emphasize enterprise features (SLA, VPC/private, KMS), per-route cost breakdowns, and performance transparency.

Recommended battle-card fields (one-line each):
- Competitor summary
- Typical customer profile
- Redwood win themes (3 bullets)
- Disadvantage to call out (if any)
- Suggested collateral to share (benchmarks, case study, pricing example)
pricing_guidance:
Principles:
- Be transparent: lead with committed Dedicated pricing for predictable throughput, and usage-based pricing for Hosted.
- Tie discounts to business outcomes: ARR committed, term length, and forecasted throughput.
- Keep standard enterprise concessions limited to security/compliance and integration timelines.

Standard packaging (examples):
- Hosted (self-serve): pay-as-you-go per-token generation + per-embedding. Free credits for initial evaluation.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): monthly/annual commit with tiers (S, M, L) mapped to GPU pools and guaranteed throughput/SLA. Includes priority support and automatic autoscale policies.
- Private: licensing fee + annual support, professional services for on-prem/VPC setup, options for higher retention/longer audit logs.

Discount & negotiation guidance:
- Volume discounts: 10-30% depending on committed spend and term.
- Enterprise add-ons (observability retention, compliance): price separately; avoid bundling into base discount.
- POC pricing: short-term discounted Dedicated or Hosted credits with clear success criteria and an agreed handoff to production terms.

Pricing examples to share with prospects (numbers illustrative):
| Package | Typical customer | Example commitment | Expected benefits |
| Hosted pay-as-you-go | Startups, dev teams | $0 up-front | Low time-to-value, pay per usage |
| Dedicated S (monthly) | Growth SaaS | $15k/month | Predictable throughput, 99.9% uptime, lower unit cost |
| Private (license + PS) | Regulated enterprise | $200k license + $50k PS | VPC/on-prem, KMS/HSM, audit-ready logs |

Approval & escalation:
- Deals with non-standard security/compliance asks escalate to Security & Compliance and Customer Success for a joint review.
- Pricing exceptions > 25% discount require VP approval.
pitch_deck_outline:
Use this outline for a 12-slide executive deck. Keep each slide visual, with a single primary takeaway.

Slides:
1) Title & ask  one-sentence ask (POC, evaluation, procurement timeline).
2) Executive summary  Redwood in one line + three value bullets (performance, cost, compliance).
3) Customer problem  common pain: unpredictable latency, high per-token cost, complex self-hosting.
4) Redwood solution overview  hosted, dedicated, private; runtime + orchestration + optimize tooling.
5) Architecture snapshot  simple diagram text: client -> API/gateway -> routing -> serving runtime (caching, batching) -> GPU fleet (dedicated/private) -> monitoring.
6) Performance & cost evidence  curated benchmarks vs public cloud / self-hosted (call out p99, throughput, unit cost improvements).
7) Security & compliance  SOC2, audit logging, KMS/HSM, VPC/private deployment.
8) Pricing & packaging  recommended offering for this prospect and proposed commitment/term.
9) Roadmap & model catalog  supported models, quantization profiles, and upcoming features relevant to prospect.
10) Case study highlight  1-2 slide callouts (metrics & outcomes).
11) Migration & success plan  PoC success criteria, timeline (4-8 weeks), roles (SE, CSM, infra).
12) Ask & next steps  clear decision points, trial details, and contact information.

Speaker notes: include callouts for each slide with suggested one-liners, top demo scenarios, and backup data references. Keep appendix with detailed benchmarks and ADRs for SRE/security teams.
case_studies:
1) FintechScale (mid-market financial services)  use case: regulatory document summarization + secure chat for internal analysts. Outcome: migrated from self-hosted runtime to Redwood Private; reduced per-query latency by 40% and improved throughput 3x. Key wins: KMS integration, audit log retention customization, and a successful SOC2 readout. Quote: "Redwood gave us enterprise controls without the multi-month ops burden."

2) ChatShop (SaaS startup)  use case: customer support chat with embeddings + reranking. Outcome: used Redwood Dedicated; reduced unit inference cost by 2.6x via KV caching and intelligent batching while improving median latency by 30ms for typical customer flows. Implementation time: 2 weeks for initial POC, full rollout in 6 weeks.

Case study collateral to share: short PDF one-pager, 5-minute customer testimonial video, and technical appendix with traffic patterns and config snippets.
security_faq:
Audience: technical buyers and security reviewers. Keep answers concise and link to full security documentation where appropriate.

Q: What compliance certifications does Redwood maintain?
A: Redwood maintains SOC2 Type II and is working toward ISO 27001. For Private deployments, customers can run with their own audit processes; we provide evidence packages and controls mapping.

Q: How is customer data isolated?
A: Multi-tenancy model explained: Hosted isolates at the tenant layer, Dedicated provides reserved GPU pools with network isolation, and Private gives full customer-managed networking and optionally air-gapped on-prem.

Q: How are secrets and keys managed?
A: We integrate with customer KMS/HSM providers (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault) and offer bring-your-own-key options for Private deployments.

Q: Is data encrypted in transit and at rest?
A: Yes. We use TLS 1.2+ in transit and AES-256 for data at rest. For Private, encryption configuration can be driven by customer policies.

Q: Can we keep inference inputs/outputs from leaving our VPC?
A: Yes. Private deployments support VPC-only access patterns and on-prem packaging. For Dedicated we offer private peering and dedicated network options.

Q: How does Redwood handle incident response?
A: We maintain an incident response runbook, 24/7 on-call rotations, and customer-facing comms procedures. For Dedicated and Private customers we provide an escalation SLA and dedicated support channels.

Q: What audit and logging capabilities are available?
A: Per-request audit logs, token-level billing traces, and configurable retention windows. Enterprise add-ons include longer retention and SIEM integration (Syslog/S3 delivery).

Q: Do you allow security assessments and penetration tests?
A: Yes. We coordinate assessments and provide redacted evidence. For Private deployments customers may run their own pentests; we provide guidance and a coordination channel.
sales_playbook_steps:
1) Discovery: qualify latency, throughput, compliance, and cost goals. Capture SLOs, traffic patterns, and compliance constraints.
2) Solution mapping: recommend hosted vs dedicated vs private and propose hardware profile + model variants.
3) POC plan: define success criteria, data/sample prompts, timeline (2-8 weeks), and ownership.
4) Security review: provide evidence pack, schedule security sync, and confirm encryption/KMS needs.
5) Pricing & procurement: present package, negotiate committed spend/terms, and align legal/SOW.
6) Onboarding & rollout: SE-led deployment, canary rollouts, performance tuning, and CSM-led adoption plan.
7) Post-sale: quarterly business reviews, cost/latency optimizations, and quality guardrail monitoring.
